title: Advanced DevOps Interview Preparation — Revised Edition

topics.name: AWS (EC2, VPC, IAM, S3, EKS, etc.)

questions.question: Your Jenkins queue has 80 builds, but CPU utilization is low. How do you isolate the bottleneck?
questions.interview_answer: Inspect queue causes, label matching, offline agents, executor limits, cloud-agent provisioning, throttling, and quiet periods. Low controller CPU does not prove agent capacity is available.
questions.technical_explanation: Use the queue item details and node/agent status first; compare required labels with online agent labels. Check provisioning logs before adding executors.
questions.production_scenario: A label mismatch or offline cloud template can leave jobs queued while CPU is idle.
questions.commands_checks: `Manage Jenkins` queue and nodes; `kubectl get pods -n jenkins` if agents run on Kubernetes; agent provisioning logs
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: What evidence distinguishes a label mismatch from a failed dynamic-agent provision?

questions.question: A pipeline stays in SCM checkout for 15 minutes. What would you check?
questions.interview_answer: Check agent connectivity, DNS, Git server reachability, credential validity, repository size, submodules, LFS, and Git client/plugin logs. Compare the same checkout from a clean agent.
questions.technical_explanation: Use a bounded timeout, inspect the exact Git command and exit output, and test DNS/TCP/TLS separately. Avoid disabling host-key verification as a quick fix.
questions.production_scenario: A slow checkout can be a network, credential, SCM, or repository problem; restarting Jenkins is not a diagnosis.
questions.commands_checks: `git ls-remote`; `GIT_CURL_VERBOSE=1` where safe; Jenkins console log; agent logs
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: How would you distinguish a credential failure from an MTU or network timeout?

questions.question: A pull request from a fork changes the Jenkinsfile and attempts to print credentials. How do you protect the pipeline?
questions.interview_answer: Treat PR code as untrusted. Do not expose deployment credentials or trusted shared-library capabilities to it; isolate agents and use separate validation and release jobs.
questions.technical_explanation: Masking is not a security boundary. Restrict credential scope, avoid privileged agents, protect branch policies, and ensure release credentials are available only after trusted review.
questions.production_scenario: A malicious pipeline can exfiltrate secrets without printing them, so log masking alone is insufficient.
questions.commands_checks: Jenkins credential usage audit; job permissions; SCM branch protection; agent isolation checks
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: How would you safely test a PR while still running useful integration tests?

questions.question: A shared-library update causes failures across 30 pipelines. What is your response?
questions.interview_answer: Freeze rollout, pin or revert to a known-good library revision, compare the failing change, and test the fix in representative pipelines before promoting it.
questions.technical_explanation: Version shared libraries, use code review and automated tests, maintain compatibility contracts, and stage library releases. Avoid changing a global default without a rollback path.
questions.production_scenario: Unpinned libraries create non-reproducible builds and large blast radius.
questions.commands_checks: Shared-library SCM revision; replay or test job logs; Git diff; representative pipeline test suite
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: How would you introduce a breaking library API without stopping all teams?

questions.question: A build log masks an AWS key, but the build has outbound network access. Is the secret safe?
questions.interview_answer: No. A process with access to a secret may encode and transmit it. Reduce access at the source, isolate untrusted jobs, use temporary credentials, and audit egress.
questions.technical_explanation: Scope credentials to the smallest stage, prefer role federation/short-lived credentials, restrict network egress where practical, and rotate any exposed credential.
questions.production_scenario: Masking prevents accidental display; it does not prevent malicious code from reading a secret.
questions.commands_checks: Jenkins credential bindings; IAM/CloudTrail audit; egress controls
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: What would you do immediately if you suspect exfiltration?

questions.question: Builds fail with no space left on device on one agent pool. How do you resolve and prevent it?
questions.interview_answer: Inspect filesystem and inode usage, workspaces, Docker layers, caches, and retained artifacts. Clean only known disposable data, then set retention and capacity controls.
questions.technical_explanation: Use workspace cleanup, image pruning with safeguards, artifact retention policies, disk alerts, and ephemeral agents when appropriate. Do not delete active build data blindly.
questions.production_scenario: A filesystem can run out of inodes even when free GB remain.
questions.commands_checks: `df -h`; `df -i`; `du -xhd1`; `docker system df`; agent workspace inspection
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: How would you tell whether workspace growth or Docker layers are responsible?

questions.question: A Java build succeeds on one Jenkins agent and fails on another. What do you compare?
questions.interview_answer: Compare JDK/Maven versions, environment variables, locale, filesystem permissions, dependency resolution, cache state, and architecture. Reproduce with a clean, pinned toolchain.
questions.technical_explanation: Use tool installers or containerized build agents, pin dependencies, archive test reports, and avoid relying on mutable agent state.
questions.production_scenario: A warm cache can hide missing or non-reproducible dependencies.
questions.commands_checks: `java -version`; `mvn -version`; `env` with secrets redacted; compare toolchain image digests
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: How would you make the build reproducible across ephemeral agents?

questions.question: QA passed, but production behaves differently even though the team says it deployed the same version. What do you verify?
questions.interview_answer: Verify artifact identity by immutable digest/checksum, configuration, secrets, feature flags, and environment differences. Promote the same built artifact instead of rebuilding it for production.
questions.technical_explanation: Record build provenance, SBOM, commit SHA, image digest, and deployment metadata. Separate configuration from artifact content.
questions.production_scenario: A mutable tag such as `latest` does not prove artifact identity.
questions.commands_checks: `docker image inspect`; registry digest; build metadata; deployment manifests
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: What evidence proves the production image is exactly the tested image?

questions.question: A 10% canary shows elevated p95 latency but normal average latency. What should the pipeline do?
questions.interview_answer: Stop traffic progression and compare canary versus baseline by route, region, and workload. Use percentile and error-rate thresholds tied to the service SLO; investigate before proceeding.
questions.technical_explanation: Use automated analysis windows, minimum sample sizes, clear rollback triggers, and a manual override with audit trail. Averages can hide tail latency regressions.
questions.production_scenario: Readiness alone cannot detect all user-visible regressions.
questions.commands_checks: Canary dashboards; request histogram metrics; deployment controller status; error logs
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: How would you avoid rolling back on noise from a low-traffic canary?

questions.question: A release includes a schema change that breaks the previous application version. How do you redesign the deployment?
questions.interview_answer: Use expand-and-contract: add backward-compatible schema first, deploy compatible application versions, migrate data, then remove obsolete schema only after old versions are gone.
questions.technical_explanation: Treat schema migration as its own controlled change with backup/restore testing, bounded locks, and rollback compatibility. App rollback may not reverse data changes.
questions.production_scenario: A binary rollback does not necessarily roll back a database migration.
questions.commands_checks: Migration logs; DB lock/latency metrics; application compatibility tests
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: How would you handle a long-running backfill with production traffic?

questions.question: A plugin update is required to fix a vulnerability. How do you upgrade safely?
questions.interview_answer: Review the advisory and dependency matrix, test the core/plugin combination in staging, back up configuration and job data, schedule a maintenance window, then validate critical jobs.
questions.technical_explanation: Prefer supported LTS for stable enterprise controllers, keep plugins minimal, and define a rollback/restore plan. A controller backup does not automatically back up external agents or artifact stores.
questions.production_scenario: Blindly updating every plugin can create incompatibilities or increase downtime.
questions.commands_checks: Jenkins changelog; plugin manager; controller logs; backup verification
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: What is your recovery path if the controller fails to start after the update?

questions.question: A pipeline sometimes hangs forever while waiting for a downstream service. How do you improve it?
questions.interview_answer: Set stage-level and overall timeouts, configure client connection/read timeouts, bound retries with backoff, and make cleanup run on failure or abort.
questions.technical_explanation: Use `timeout`, `retry` only for transient failures, and `post { always { ... } }` for cleanup. Ensure retries do not duplicate non-idempotent actions.
questions.production_scenario: Unbounded retries can amplify an outage and consume agents.
questions.commands_checks: Jenkinsfile `timeout`; service client timeout settings; console timestamps
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: How would you retry an idempotent GET differently from a payment operation?

questions.question: A test suite fails only when tests run in parallel. How do you investigate?
questions.interview_answer: Look for shared mutable state, port/file collisions, database fixtures, race conditions, rate limits, and test ordering. Reproduce with controlled concurrency before disabling parallelism permanently.
questions.technical_explanation: Use isolated test data and namespaces, deterministic fixtures, and quarantine only with an owner and deadline.
questions.production_scenario: Rerunning until green hides flakiness rather than fixing it.
questions.commands_checks: Test reports; process/resource metrics; repeat runs at controlled concurrency
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: How would you determine whether the cause is application code or test infrastructure?

questions.question: A Git webhook says delivered, but Jenkins does not start a job. What do you check?
questions.interview_answer: Verify webhook endpoint reachability, authentication/secret, repository/job association, event type, branch filters, plugin health, and controller logs.
questions.technical_explanation: Test delivery IDs and timestamps, avoid exposing webhook secrets, and alert on webhook failures and stale SCM polling.
questions.production_scenario: A successful HTTP response does not prove the expected job matched the event.
questions.commands_checks: SCM webhook delivery log; Jenkins system log; job trigger configuration
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: What would you check if only tag pushes fail to trigger?

questions.question: A blue-green release passes health checks but user sessions fail after switching traffic. How do you respond?
questions.interview_answer: Shift traffic back if safe, inspect session/state compatibility and sticky-session assumptions, then test the rollback path. Check shared database/cache changes and connection draining.
questions.technical_explanation: Blue-green isolates application versions, not necessarily shared data or external dependencies. Make sessions compatible or externalize them safely.
questions.production_scenario: Traffic rollback may not restore state changed by the new version.
questions.commands_checks: Load balancer target groups; session store metrics; app logs; deployment timeline
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: What pre-release test would expose session incompatibility?

questions.question: A developer can deploy to production by manually rerunning a job, bypassing approval. How do you close the gap?
questions.interview_answer: Enforce authorization at the deployment boundary, not only in UI conventions. Restrict job permissions, credentials, protected branches, and cloud IAM so unapproved jobs cannot deploy.
questions.technical_explanation: Separate build and deploy roles; require auditable approvals and protect pipeline definitions. Test negative authorization paths.
questions.production_scenario: A visual approval step is not an access-control boundary if credentials remain accessible elsewhere.
questions.commands_checks: Jenkins role matrix; folder permissions; IAM role trust; audit logs
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: How would you prevent a compromised agent from reusing deployment credentials?

questions.question: A shared dependency cache may have been modified by an untrusted build. What do you do?
questions.interview_answer: Stop trusting the cache, isolate or purge affected cache entries, verify artifact checksums/signatures, and rebuild in a clean environment.
questions.technical_explanation: Separate caches by trust level, validate dependencies with lockfiles/checksums, and avoid letting untrusted PR jobs write caches used by releases.
questions.production_scenario: Caches are performance optimizations, not sources of truth.
questions.commands_checks: Cache backend ACLs; dependency checksum verification; build provenance
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: How would you balance cache isolation against build duration?

questions.question: Ephemeral agent Pods disappear during builds. How do you diagnose it?
questions.interview_answer: Inspect Pod events, node pressure, eviction reason, agent pod template, service account permissions, and connectivity to the controller. Check whether jobs tolerate preemption or interruptions.
questions.technical_explanation: Set realistic resource requests, preserve logs, use retry only for safe build steps, and configure pod retention for failed agents during diagnosis.
questions.production_scenario: Restarting the controller may not address node eviction or Pod scheduling issues.
questions.commands_checks: `kubectl get pods -n jenkins`; `kubectl describe pod`; Jenkins Kubernetes plugin logs
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: What changes if Pods show OOMKilled versus Evicted?

questions.question: How would you prove a production artifact came from an approved source commit and pipeline?
questions.interview_answer: Record immutable artifact digest, source revision, builder identity, build metadata, SBOM, and signed provenance; verify policy at deployment.
questions.technical_explanation: Protect build infrastructure and signing keys, separate duties, and fail closed when verification is required but absent.
questions.production_scenario: A signed image proves the signer signed it, not by itself that the build process was trustworthy.
questions.commands_checks: Image digest; SBOM; signature/provenance verification; CI attestation
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: What trust assumptions must be validated in the build system?

questions.question: The controller disk is lost. What must be restored and how do you validate recovery?
questions.interview_answer: Restore a tested backup of Jenkins home/configuration and required secrets, reconnect agents and external artifact/SCM services, then validate critical jobs and credentials.
questions.technical_explanation: Document RPO/RTO, encrypt backups, keep copies isolated, and test restores regularly. Include plugin/version compatibility and external dependencies.
questions.production_scenario: Backup manifest; restore test; controller logs; representative pipeline smoke tests
questions.commands_checks: Inspect relevant logs, configuration, health metrics, and recent change history; use the topic guide's diagnostic commands as a starting point.
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: A backup job success does not prove a complete recovery is possible.

questions.question: A critical security fix must ship during a release freeze. How do you manage it?
questions.interview_answer: Use the documented emergency change process, narrow the change, run risk-based tests and security checks, obtain authorized approval, deploy progressively, and monitor after release.
questions.technical_explanation: Maintain auditable emergency approvals and follow-up review; do not permanently bypass standard controls.
questions.production_scenario: Change record; pipeline approvals; test evidence; monitoring dashboards
questions.commands_checks: Inspect relevant logs, configuration, health metrics, and recent change history; use the topic guide's diagnostic commands as a starting point.
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: A release freeze should control risk, not block necessary incident response without a defined exception.

questions.question: A container image layer contains a deleted `.env` file. Is the secret removed?
questions.interview_answer: No. Image layers can retain deleted content. Revoke/rotate the secret, rebuild from a clean context, remove sensitive files from history/layers, and scan the final image.
questions.technical_explanation: Use build secrets mechanisms and `.dockerignore`; do not copy credentials into image layers at all.
questions.production_scenario: `docker history`; image scanning; registry digest; secret rotation audit
questions.commands_checks: Inspect relevant logs, configuration, health metrics, and recent change history; use the topic guide's diagnostic commands as a starting point.
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: Deleting a file in a later Docker layer does not erase it from earlier layers.

questions.question: How would you design access for developers, release managers, and administrators?
questions.interview_answer: Apply least privilege by role and folder, separate build from production deployment, restrict credential domains, and audit privileged changes.
questions.technical_explanation: Use SSO/MFA where available, protect admin accounts, and review plugin permissions. Avoid shared administrator accounts.
questions.production_scenario: Jenkins authorization strategy; folder/job permissions; audit logs
questions.commands_checks: Inspect relevant logs, configuration, health metrics, and recent change history; use the topic guide's diagnostic commands as a starting point.
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: Job-level access can still expose secrets through pipeline modification if trust boundaries are wrong.

questions.question: A build fails but Jenkins shows no test report. What do you check?
questions.interview_answer: Determine whether tests ran, whether the report path matches the workspace, whether the publisher executes after failure, and whether the agent was lost before archiving.
questions.technical_explanation: Archive diagnostic output in `post { always { ... } }` where safe and preserve test exit codes.
questions.production_scenario: Console log; workspace listing; `archiveArtifacts`; test report publisher config
questions.commands_checks: Inspect relevant logs, configuration, health metrics, and recent change history; use the topic guide's diagnostic commands as a starting point.
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: Marking a build successful just to publish reports destroys the signal from test failures.

questions.question: Two pipeline runs deploy different commits to the same environment simultaneously. How do you prevent it?
questions.interview_answer: Serialize deployments per environment or use a deployment controller with concurrency controls, and ensure the deployed revision is explicit and auditable.
questions.technical_explanation: Use Jenkins `disableConcurrentBuilds()` when appropriate, environment locks, and optimistic checks; avoid global serialization if it unnecessarily blocks independent environments.
questions.production_scenario: Pipeline concurrency settings; deployment audit trail; environment lock state
questions.commands_checks: Inspect relevant logs, configuration, health metrics, and recent change history; use the topic guide's diagnostic commands as a starting point.
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: Locking only a Jenkins job may not protect against another pipeline or external deployment tool.

questions.question: A team claims rollback is supported, but the previous image cannot run against the new schema. What changes?
questions.interview_answer: Make schema evolution backward-compatible, keep prior artifacts available, test rollback in staging, and define forward-fix options when data changes are irreversible.
questions.technical_explanation: Document recovery and data migration strategies; do not equate deployment controller rollback with application/data rollback.
questions.production_scenario: Schema compatibility tests; artifact retention; rollback drill
questions.commands_checks: Inspect relevant logs, configuration, health metrics, and recent change history; use the topic guide's diagnostic commands as a starting point.
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: Rollback plans must include stateful dependencies, not only the application image.

questions.question: A dependency registry is compromised. What controls reduce impact?
questions.interview_answer: Pin dependencies, verify checksums/signatures where available, use controlled mirrors, scan packages, generate SBOMs, and restrict build network access.
questions.technical_explanation: Use reproducible builds and monitor dependency changes; rotate credentials if the build environment may have been exposed.
questions.production_scenario: Lockfiles; package integrity metadata; SBOM diff; registry logs
questions.commands_checks: Inspect relevant logs, configuration, health metrics, and recent change history; use the topic guide's diagnostic commands as a starting point.
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: A vulnerability scanner alone may not detect a malicious but non-vulnerable package.

questions.question: A vulnerable plugin is installed but removing it may break pipelines. What is the decision process?
questions.interview_answer: Assess exploitability and exposure, identify affected jobs and dependencies, test upgrade/removal in staging, apply mitigations, and document a time-bound risk acceptance if immediate remediation is impossible.
questions.technical_explanation: Reduce controller exposure, restrict admin access, and prioritize supported fixed versions. Avoid leaving an exception without an owner and deadline.
questions.production_scenario: Security advisory; plugin dependency graph; staging test results
questions.commands_checks: Inspect relevant logs, configuration, health metrics, and recent change history; use the topic guide's diagnostic commands as a starting point.
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: A plugin's apparent lack of use does not prove it is unreachable or harmless.

questions.question: A pipeline uses `node:latest` and starts failing after an upstream image update. What should change?
questions.interview_answer: Pin a tested image version or digest, update deliberately, scan the image, and promote the exact tested build image through environments.
questions.technical_explanation: Automate update PRs and compatibility tests instead of freezing dependencies forever.
questions.production_scenario: Docker image digest; CI config diff; build provenance
questions.commands_checks: Inspect relevant logs, configuration, health metrics, and recent change history; use the topic guide's diagnostic commands as a starting point.
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: Pinning without a patch/update process can leave known vulnerabilities unaddressed.

questions.question: A stage times out during a temporary API slowdown. How do you set a meaningful timeout?
questions.interview_answer: Derive timeout from service latency distributions, expected workload, and SLO; bound retries and distinguish connection from read timeouts.
questions.technical_explanation: Use metrics to tune timeouts and add jittered backoff only for retry-safe operations.
questions.production_scenario: Stage duration metrics; dependency latency percentiles; timeout logs
questions.commands_checks: Inspect relevant logs, configuration, health metrics, and recent change history; use the topic guide's diagnostic commands as a starting point.
questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: Simply increasing every timeout can hide a degraded dependency.

questions.question: A deployment works from a laptop but not from Jenkins. What environment differences do you inspect?
questions.interview_answer: Compare runtime/tool versions, environment variables, file permissions, network routes, credentials, working directory, locale, and secret injection.
questions.technical_explanation: Make toolchains explicit and keep configuration reproducible; redact secrets when comparing environment output.
questions.production_scenario: `env` with sensitive values removed; tool version commands; agent image digest

questions.follow_up: Copying an entire local environment into CI can introduce secrets and hidden dependencies.

questions.question: The UI is slow and job scheduling lags. How do you separate controller pressure from agent capacity?
questions.interview_answer: Check controller CPU/memory/GC, thread dumps, queue causes, plugin activity, disk I/O, and agent provisioning. Move builds off controller and reduce expensive synchronous work.
questions.technical_explanation: Scale agents for build capacity, not controller executor count alone; upgrade only after profiling and compatibility checks.
questions.production_scenario: Jenkins metrics; thread dump; GC logs; queue and agent telemetry

questions.common_mistake: Changing several variables at once, relying on one green status, or making an irreversible change before verifying the failure domain.
questions.follow_up: Adding agents does not fix controller thread exhaustion or plugin deadlocks.

questions.question: Pipeline failures are not reaching the on-call channel. What is your response?
questions.interview_answer: Check notification stage execution, credentials, endpoint health, rate limits, retries, and failure paths. Use an independent alert for notification-system failure.
questions.technical_explanation: Keep notification failure visible without masking the primary build result; test delivery and escalation regularly.
questions.production_scenario: Pipeline `post` logs; webhook response; alert delivery audit

questions.follow_up: A failed notification must not silently convert a failed build into a success.

questions.interview_answer: Use structured commit/PR metadata and verified merged changes, link tickets, and allow review for breaking changes and security disclosures.
questions.technical_explanation: Generate drafts automatically but do not rely on commit messages alone as authoritative user-facing documentation.

questions.question: What repository controls should be required before a production deployment?
questions.interview_answer: Require reviewed changes, successful required checks, protected release branches/tags, and restricted deploy identities. Ensure administrators and bots are covered by appropriate policies.
questions.technical_explanation: Use signed commits/tags where required, audit bypasses, and keep CI permissions read-only unless needed.

questions.interview_answer: Compare stage timings, queue time, dependency download time, test parallelism, cache hit rate, and agent resource metrics before changing capacity.

questions.question: How do you choose artifact retention without losing the ability to recover?
questions.interview_answer: Set retention according to release cadence, audit obligations, rollback window, and storage cost; preserve production release artifacts and metadata longer than disposable CI outputs.
questions.technical_explanation: Use immutable artifact repositories, lifecycle policies, and restore/availability checks.

questions.question: A repository update triggers hundreds of duplicate builds. How do you reduce noise safely?
questions.interview_answer: Inspect webhook and branch indexing behavior, duplicate triggers, PR discovery settings, and downstream triggers. Debounce only where it preserves required validation.
questions.technical_explanation: Tune branch discovery and concurrency; retain required checks for protected branches and releases.

questions.question: The deploy job deploys a newer commit than the approved build. How do you prevent this?
questions.interview_answer: Pass an immutable artifact identifier and source revision from build to deploy, verify approval refers to that artifact, and reject mismatches.
